## Your team is already using AI. Do you know where your client files are going?

Someone in your office has already pasted a client documents into a chatbot to save twenty minutes. They meant well. But that text now sits on a server you don't control, under terms you never read.

Banning AI doesn't work; people use it on their phones instead. And the firms down the street are getting faster. You need a way to say yes to AI without gambling with your clients' trust.

## Not all your data needs the same protection.

Cloud AI from the big providers is more capable than anything you can run in your office, and you should use it wherever your rules allow. Client information is different. So we sort your data into three tiers, and each tier gets the right tool.

### Public

Your website, marketing and anything already published.

Runs on

Any approved AI tool

### Internal

Firm operations with no client details: budgets, procedures, templates.

Runs on

Approved cloud AI, under business terms

### Client confidential

Anything about a client's affairs.

Runs on

Your own computer, in your office

This is the same approach a security officer uses in a large company. We set it up for a firm of five.

## A private AI system you own, and the rules to run it.

### Private AI on your own hardware

Open-weight AI models running on a dedicated Apple computer in your office. Nothing goes to an AI vendor.

### Access that matches your files

Each person signs in with their work account and sees only the client folders they can already open.

### A written AI use policy

Clear rules on what data goes where, approved tools, and what to do if something goes wrong. Your team is trained on it.

### Models chosen on your work

We test leading open models on your own anonymized documents for accuracy, citations and speed before you commit.

### One live automation

For example: every new document in a client folder gets summarized, with dates and deadlines flagged for review.

### A roadmap you own

A plan for what to automate next, a runbook for upkeep, and full admin control at handover.

## What on-premise AI does, and what it doesn't.

You're trusting us with your clients' confidence, so here it is plainly.

### What it does

-   Keeps client information on hardware in your office.
-   Removes the risk of an AI vendor storing or training on your data.
-   Lets you prove it: outbound connections are blocked except software updates.
-   Gives each person access only to the files they're entitled to.

### What it doesn't do

-   It doesn't make you compliant on its own. Your professional obligations still apply, and your policy and people carry most of the weight.
-   It isn't as capable as the best cloud AI. Local models are good, not perfect, so every answer cites its source and a professional reviews it.
-   It isn't legal or regulatory advice. You make the final call on your obligations.

### Under the hood (for your IT advisor)

Hardware

Apple Mac Studio or Mac mini, sized to your documents and team. Encrypted disk, battery backup.

Models

Open-weight models such as Qwen, Gemma and gpt-oss, chosen by testing on your documents

Software

Ollama and Open WebUI, both open source. No lock-in.

Sign-in

Microsoft 365 single sign-on with multi-factor authentication

Network

No inbound access from the internet; outbound blocked except updates; remote access by VPN

Isolation

Supporting services in sandboxed containers with access only to the folders they need

Recovery

Nightly encrypted backup to a location you control

## Is this right for your firm?

### This is for you if

-   You run a firm of roughly 3 to 25 people.
-   Your work involves confidential client information.
-   Your team wants to use AI, or already does.
-   You want clear rules, not a blanket ban.

### This is not for you if

-   You want AI that acts on its own, with no one reviewing its work.
-   Your client data is all in a cloud system you're happy to use AI inside. (We'll still help with the policy.)
-   You're not ready to name someone to own the system after handover.
